record.paper_title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology
record.original_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). A topological space is Baire when every countable intersection of dense open subsets is dense; it is hereditarily Baire when every non-empty closed subspace is Baire. Characterize, in terms of properties of the underlying metric space (X, d), exactly when the Wijsman hyperspace is a Baire space.

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be \emph{Baire} if the intersection of every sequence of dense open subsets of $X$ is still dense. Note that a closed subspace of a Baire space may not be Baire. A space is called \emph{hereditarily Baire} if every non-empty closed subspace is Baire.
Problem 4.1. Let (X, d) be a metric space. Find characterizations for (2^X, T_W(d)) to be a Baire space, in terms of some properties of (X, d).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and let $2^X$ denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$. For each $A \in 2^X$, let $d(\cdot, A): X \to \mathbb{R}$ be the distance functional $x \mapsto \inf_{a \in A} d(x,a)$. The Wijsman topology $\mathcal{T}_{W(d)}$ on $2^X$ is defined to be the weakest topology on $2^X$ making every functional $A \mapsto d(x,A)$ (for $x \in X$) continuous; equivalently, it is generated by the subbasic open sets $\{A \in 2^X : d(x,A) < r\}$ and $\{A \in 2^X : d(x,A) > r\}$ for $x \in X$ and $r \ge 0$. The resulting space $(2^X, \mathcal{T}_{W(d)})$ is called the Wijsman hyperspace of $(X,d)$.

Recall that a topological space is a Baire space if the intersection of every countable family of dense open subsets is dense, and is hereditarily Baire if every non-empty closed subspace is a Baire space.

Find a characterization, expressed purely in terms of properties of the metric space $(X,d)$, of when the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X, \mathcal{T}_{W(d)})$ is a Baire space.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: the Wijsman hyperspace of a complete metric space is Baire, and more generally the Wijsman hyperspace of a metric hereditarily Baire space is Baire. A characterization is available for metrizable base spaces with a countable-in-itself π-base, and examples of first-category metric spaces with Baire Wijsman hyperspace exist. However, a full characterization in terms of properties of (X,d) does not appear to be known, and in particular it remains open whether the Wijsman hyperspace of every metric Baire space is Baire.

status_evidence.title: Amsterdam properties of Wijsman hyperspaces
status_evidence.snippet: Baireness of the Wijsman hyperspace topology is characterized for a metrizable base space with a countable-in-itself π-base; a separable first category metric space is constructed with a Baire Wijsman hyperspace.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization is only known in special cases; first-category examples exist.

status_evidence.title: Note on the Wijsman Hyperspaces of Completely Metrizable Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The Wijsman hyperspace of a metric hereditarily Baire space is Baire, solving a question of Zsilinszky.
status_evidence.claim: Hereditary Baireness of (X,d) suffices for Baireness of the Wijsman hyperspace; full characterization remains unsettled.

status_evidence.title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology (arXiv:1609.03119)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 4.1. Let (X, d) be a metric space. Find characterizations for (2^X, T_W(d)) to be a Baire space, in terms of some properties of (X, d).
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as open.
